section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the term "korban" (offering) indicates an elevation from below to above, where the creature leaves its own existence to be absorbed in the Ein Sof, a nullification of utter decay.
section.t: And to add,
that this—that offerings are a matter of elevation—
is also understood from the fact that they are called by the name "korban."
[And particularly according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov48
(on the verse49
"Forever, O Lord, Your word stands firm in the heavens"),
that the name of every thing by which it is called in the Holy Tongue indicates
(not only its essence but also)
the G‑dly life-force within it].
For "korban" is from the term "kiruv" (drawing near)50,
that it draws near to G‑dliness.
And this indicates the matter of elevation.
For in a drawing down from above to below,
its connection with G‑dliness is through G‑dliness being drawn
(drawn near)
to it,
but "korban" from the term "kiruv"
(that it draws near to G‑dliness)
means
that it goes out from its place
(its existence)
and is included in G‑dliness.
And one may connect this with what is said in Likkutei Torah51,
that "lehakriv" (to offer) is the letters of "leharikiv" (to cause to rot),
for decay is utter nullification.
And the explanation of this can be said,
that the elevation of offerings is to the Ein Sof that is beyond any relation to worlds52,
[and beyond this,
that the elevation of offerings is upward without end,
as stated in Pri Etz Chayim53,
that it is brought in the Zohar54
"Until where does the will of offerings ascend? ... upward, upward, until Ein Sof"],
and therefore the nullification of offerings is a nullification of decay,
utter nullification.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the parallel in the soul's service of offerings through prayer, where the soul's descent is for the purpose of ascending and being included in the Ein Sof, leading to utter self-nullification.
section.t: And similarly is it in the service of offerings within the soul of man55,
"When a man among you brings an offering,"
that the descent of the soul below is for the sake of ascent,
so that there should be the matter of elevation from below to above,
to go out from its existence and be included in the Ein Sof.
And its ascent is in prayer,
for they instituted prayers corresponding to the offerings56.
And according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov57,
that this—that a person lives after prayer—is not according to nature.
For from the side of the great intentions58
that are in prayer, there should be in him a expiration of the soul,
and that he remains alive after prayer is not according to nature, but a great kindness from the Holy One, blessed be He.
And it can be said,
that this—that from the side of the great intentions in prayer one reaches
(according to nature)
expiration of the soul—
is
because prayer is the matter of elevation, to go out from one's existence and be included in the Ein Sof,
similar to the offering that was burned and included in the fire from above.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the preparation for prayer requires humility and lowliness, a nullification of distance, while the nullification during prayer is a nullification of soul-expiration through closeness to G‑dliness.
section.t: And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said59,
"One should not stand to pray except with a heavy head," and Rashi explained60,
submission and lowliness,
for since the matter of prayer is that one goes out from his existence and is included in the Ein Sof,
nullification,
therefore also the preparation for prayer is submission and lowliness,
nullification.
However, the nullification of prayer is from the side of the closeness to G‑dliness,
in which one feels the elevation and wonder of the Ein Sof, and therefore desires to be included in it,
while the nullification before prayer is that one becomes embittered over his distance from G‑dliness.
And therefore,
the nullification of prayer is a nullification of soul-expiration, that he is included in G‑dliness,
and the nullification before prayer is submission and lowliness.
And the Mitteler Rebbe explains in the maamar beginning "After the Lord your G‑d you shall walk"61,
and likewise the Tzemach Tzedek explains in his maamar beginning "This"62,
that this—that the nullification of submission and lowliness is a preparation for prayer—
is as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said63,
"Whoever lowers himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him up."
And it can be said that what is stated in Likkutei Torah, that "lehakriv" is the letters of "leharikiv," is in the manner of the nullification before prayer64,
for the nullification of decay is that one's existence is destroyed.
But through the decay, growth subsequently occurs—similar to the lowliness before prayer
(through which the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him up in prayer).
